# Welcome {.unnumbered}

<!-- Status: FIRST DRAFT (2026-10-18), front-matter agent, under the editor's delegation (D19). Pending the author's voice edit. -->

*AI for All: Career-Ready AI Skills* is a textbook about using artificial intelligence (AI) well, in study and at work. It is written for CS 2V95.001 at The University of Texas at Dallas (Spring 2027), and for anyone who wants the same skills without taking the course.

The book is for every major. You do not need to know programming, statistics or computer science. You need curiosity, a willingness to test what a tool gives you, and the habit of asking who answers for the result. The examples come from business, health, the arts and humanities, the social sciences, the natural sciences, engineering and education, so you will find your own field.

The book does not teach the menus of any one product. Products change within months. What lasts is judgment: deciding whether AI belongs in a task, checking what it produces, choosing what to keep, and saying openly how you used it.

## What Is Inside {.unnumbered}

The 23 chapters are grouped into six parts:

- **Part I, Understanding AI (Chapters 1–4):** how AI systems learn from data, how language models produce text, and how and why they fail.
- **Part II, Working with AI (Chapters 5–10):** framing tasks and prompts, learning with AI, verifying claims and sources, and writing in your own voice.
- **Part III, Deciding and Building with AI (Chapters 11–14):** decision support, choosing tools, images, audio and video, and agents under human oversight.
- **Part IV, Using AI Responsibly (Chapters 15–18):** privacy and security, bias and fairness, explainability, and intellectual property, law and governance.
- **Part V, AI in Your Field and Your Future (Chapters 19–21):** field guides, your portfolio and career narrative, and your personal code of practice.
- **Part VI, Frontiers and Big Questions (Chapters 22–23):** current developments and the philosophical debates around AI.

Every section carries one of three tags. **Core** is the required, examinable reading; **Studio** is hands-on work for the lab; **Deep** is an optional extension for readers who want more.

## Where to Start {.unnumbered}

Read "How to Use This Book" first. It explains the reading paths, the parts of every chapter, where the answers are, and which route through the book suits a student, an instructor, a self-learner or a working professional. Then read "Meet the Students" to meet the five students who travel with you through the chapters.
